title: Ayn Zubaidah: A waqf built over 1,000 years ago, still giving water to pilgrims today. @WahedInvest
description:
A spring outside Makkah still carries her name, more than a thousand years later.

In the 8th century, water in Makkah was so scarce that a single water-skin could sell for a dinar. Zubaidah bint Ja’far, wife of the Caliph Harun al-Rashid, had the money to pay for water one Hajj at a time. She chose to bring it from a spring at Wadi Nu’man, through mountains and solid rock, all the way to the city.

She was warned about the cost. As the story goes, her answer was: “Do it, even if every swing of the pickaxe costs a dinar.”

The water kept flowing to pilgrims for centuries. People still call it Ayn Zubaidah.

She built a waqf. Give once, and it keeps giving.

What is the true message of Ashura?

Many people associate Ashura with a single historical event, but its lessons span generations. From the story of Musa (AS) and his deliverance from Pharaoh, to the story of Husayn ibn Ali (RA) at Karbala, Ashura reminds us that truth, patience, justice, and steadfastness are timeless values.
